1.2.0.versionNote: 1.2.0 (8 Aug 2026): dead-branch cleanup + step-count wiring. Removed 2 rules whose entire inject lists referenced items that were never authored (os_g3_burden_trajectory -> [os_d3_reporting_growth, os_d6_burden_age]; os_d1_routine_step_count -> [os_d1_last_process_audit, os_d1_removability_test]) and pruned 4 more dead targets (os_d2_integration_quality, os_d3_reporting_growth, os_d4_key_person_absence_test, os_d5_control_removal_authority) from otherwise-live rules. No behavior change from the cleanup: these references already no-op'd in the queue guard. Companion scorer change (same date): os_d1_routine_step_count now feeds process_density (it was asked and discarded), so runs answering it score differently than under the 2026_05_14 scorer — see scorer_version. | Prior 1.1.0 (30 Jul 2026): +9 items. Five the adapter and engine already expected but the config never defined (os_d2_workaround_stability, os_d4_new_person_viability, os_d3_report_actionability, os_d6_admin_hours_weekly, os_d6_upkeep_visibility), plus four front-line counterparts reusing their parent items' option tokens (os_d1_exception_frontline, os_d3_exception_frontline_norm, os_d5_control_frontline_growth, os_d5_uncertainty_frontline). Scoring arithmetic unchanged: identical answers to the 1.0.0 items still produce the identical 1.0.0 score.

dimensions.label: Process Density
dimensions.description: Accumulated weight of steps, reviews, approvals, handoffs, and procedural requirements relative to what the underlying work requires.

dimensions.label: Systems Friction
dimensions.description: Labor and attention consumed by system switching, duplicate data entry, manual patching, and integration gaps.

dimensions.label: Reporting and Exception Burden
dimensions.description: Operating labor absorbed by reporting, oversight, proof-of-work demands, and exception handling.

dimensions.label: Workaround Dependence
dimensions.description: Degree to which execution depends on off-path effort, informal coordination, or improvised compensatory behavior.

dimensions.label: Control Load
dimensions.description: Cumulative governance weight relative to the actual risk profile and value of the work being controlled.

dimensions.label: Administrative Upkeep Burden
dimensions.description: Ongoing maintenance labor required simply to keep the administrative environment functioning.

notes.runtime_state_trigger: State keys resolve against the running engine state object and are evaluated after burden recomputation and before next-item selection.
notes.maxFirings: Scoped to the injected probe or item ID, not merely the routing rule.
notes.dedup: The engine deduplicates the queue by item ID before each render step.
notes.skipIfAnswered: If true, do not inject an item already answered earlier in the same run.

60.coverageRule: All six dimensions, deepest on top 3 active dimensions

text.operational: When you think about where work slows down or requires extra effort, what is the most common source?
text.managerial: When you think about where your team loses time or absorbs unnecessary administrative effort, what is the most common source?
text.senior_leader: When you think about where the operating environment is imposing the most burden on execution, what is the most common source?

items.scoringNote: Primary burden source is the initial gating classifier and should activate the selected dimension immediately.

text.operational: Roughly how much of your working time goes toward administrative tasks rather than directly advancing the work itself?
text.managerial: Roughly how much of your team’s time goes toward administrative tasks rather than directly advancing the work itself?
text.senior_leader: Roughly how much capacity in this environment is being absorbed by administrative tasks rather than directly advancing the work itself?

items.scoringNote: High admin time share activates upkeep burden and may also indicate hidden reporting burden.

text.operational: Over the past year, has the administrative weight of your environment gotten heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?
text.managerial: Over the past year, has the administrative burden around this workflow gotten heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?
text.senior_leader: Over the past year, has the administrative burden around this operating environment gotten heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?

items.scoringNote: Trajectory is a burden-age and growth signal rather than a direct burden dimension.

text.operational: When administrative burden absorbs time in this environment, is that cost generally visible to people who could reduce it?
text.managerial: When your team loses capacity to administrative burden, is that cost generally visible to people who could reduce it?
text.senior_leader: When administrative burden absorbs capacity in this environment, is that cost generally visible to the people who have authority to reduce it?

items.scoringNote: Hidden drag visibility suppresses confidence and increases the chance of hidden burden profile classification.

text.operational: How many distinct approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine work item typically require before it is complete?
text.managerial: How many distinct approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine work item typically require in this environment?
text.senior_leader: How many distinct approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine item typically require in this operating environment?

items.scoringNote: High step count is a direct process-density indicator.

text.managerial: How often do exceptions or escalations become part of the normal path rather than the routine path?
text.senior_leader: How common is exception handling relative to the routine path in this environment?

items.scoringNote: High exception ratio cross-loads into reporting and exception burden.

text.operational: How many separate systems or tools does a person typically touch to complete one unit of work in this environment?
text.managerial: How many separate systems or tools does your team typically touch to complete one unit of work in this environment?
text.senior_leader: How many distinct systems or tools are typically involved in moving one unit of work through this environment?

items.scoringNote: System count increases friction exposure but should be interpreted together with design quality.

text.operational: How often does completing work require re-entering information that already exists somewhere else in the system?
text.managerial: How often does your team have to re-enter information that already exists elsewhere in the system environment?
text.senior_leader: How often does this environment require duplicate data entry across systems?

items.scoringNote: Duplicate entry is a direct signal of systems friction and may activate contradiction probe C3 in combination with low system count.

text.operational: How many hours per week does a typical person in this environment spend on status reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?
text.managerial: How many hours per week does a typical team member spend on status reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?
text.senior_leader: How many hours per week does a typical person in this environment spend on reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?

items.scoringNote: High reporting hours are a primary direct measure of reporting burden.

text.managerial: Has exception handling become normalized enough that it now behaves like part of the standard operating load?
text.senior_leader: Has exception processing become normalized enough that it now behaves like part of the baseline operating design?

items.scoringNote: High exception normalization combined with flat trajectory activates chronic normalization contradiction logic.

text.operational: How often do people have to manually follow up just to keep work moving?
text.managerial: How often does your team have to manually follow up just to keep work moving?
text.senior_leader: How often does this environment depend on manual follow-up simply to preserve movement?

items.scoringNote: Manual follow-up is one half of contradiction probe C1 and should remain distinct from off-path work.

text.operational: How often does getting work done require steps or contacts that are not part of the official process?
text.managerial: How often does your team rely on off-path effort or informal coordination to get work done?
text.senior_leader: How often does this environment depend on off-path effort or informal coordination to preserve output?

items.scoringNote: High off-path work is a primary workaround dependence signal and pairs with manual follow-up in contradiction probe C1.

text.operational: For the work in this environment, does the governance and control overhead feel proportionate to the actual risk or compliance need?
text.managerial: Does the governance and control overhead around this work feel proportionate to the actual risk or compliance need?
text.senior_leader: Does the current governance and control overhead appear proportionate to the actual risk and value profile of the work?

options.label: Much heavier than the risk warrants

items.scoringNote: Governance fit is the primary control-load proportionality test and one half of contradiction probe C2.

text.managerial: When new controls or oversight requirements are added, how often are existing ones removed to compensate?
text.senior_leader: When new controls or oversight requirements are added, how often are existing ones removed to compensate?

items.scoringNote: Control add/remove asymmetry is the bias half of contradiction probe C2.

text.senior_leader: When uncertainty appears, what is the institution’s default first response?

items.scoringNote: Senior leader directional control-bias probe that can also surface C2 directly.

text.operational: How much of the weekly administrative workload here is upkeep rather than work that advances outcomes?
text.managerial: How much of the weekly administrative workload in this environment is upkeep rather than work that advances outcomes?
text.senior_leader: How much of the weekly administrative workload in this environment is upkeep rather than work that advances outcomes?

options.label: Upkeep takes more time than expected

items.scoringNote: Upkeep share is the first direct burden framing question for D6.

text.operational: When work requires off-path effort, does that usually involve follow-up steps that would not show in the formal process?
text.managerial: Does your team’s off-path effort often happen outside what the formal workflow would record as follow-up?
text.senior_leader: Is it possible the informal effort sustaining this workflow is not visible in formal workflow records?

options.label: No, the formal and informal routes are reasonably aligned

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for visible/invisible labor split.

text.operational: Even when the process seems broadly reasonable, is the normal response to uncertainty still to add another check, step, or approval?
text.managerial: Even where governance appears generally proportionate, does your environment still default to adding new oversight more easily than removing old oversight?
text.senior_leader: Even where leaders describe governance as right-sized, is the institution’s default response to uncertainty still to add control rather than redesign the workflow?

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for framing-versus-behavior gap in control load.

text.operational: If the number of systems is not especially high, is the real problem how those systems are designed, connected, or used in practice?
text.managerial: Does the friction seem to come less from system count and more from weak integration, poor workflow design, or manual bridging between systems?
text.senior_leader: Is the technology burden in this environment being driven more by design quality and integration gaps than by the sheer number of systems involved?

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for design-quality versus system-count mismatch.

text.operational: Could the real burden here be heavier than it appears because some of the extra effort is simply treated as normal work?
text.managerial: Is it possible your team is absorbing more administrative burden than leadership can clearly see because it is hidden inside normal delivery expectations?
text.senior_leader: Could this environment be materially heavier in practice than current signals suggest because the upkeep cost is not visible in capacity accounting?

items.scoringNote: Scoring-layer contradiction probe. Evaluate only after burden recomputation and before next-item selection.

text.operational: Has this level of exception handling been part of the job long enough that it no longer stands out as unusual?
text.managerial: Has recurring exception handling become normalized enough that the team now treats it as standard operating load rather than a signal of workflow weakness?
text.senior_leader: Has exception processing become so routine that the organization now experiences it as baseline operating design rather than a condition worth correcting?

items.scoringNote: Contradiction probe for flat trajectory plus normalized exception burden.

text.operational: When work goes off the official path, is the workaround itself consistent — or does it depend on who is doing it that day?
text.managerial: When your team works around the official process, is that workaround consistent across people — or does each person improvise their own?
text.senior_leader: Where execution departs from the documented process, is the deviation standardised in practice — or does it vary by individual?

options.label: The official path is followed; no informal knowledge needed
There is a workaround, but everyone uses the same one
It varies noticeably from person to person
It is improvised more or less every time
The documented process and the real one have simply parted ways

items.scoringNote: Feeds instructionVariance via mapInstructionVariance in legacy-adapter.v1.js, which reads this id directly. Option tokens are fixed by that mapping and must not be renamed. Dimension is workaround_dependence on substance; the d2 prefix is retained because the adapter references this exact id.

text.operational: If someone new joined tomorrow and followed only the written process, would the work actually get through?
text.managerial: If a new team member followed only the documented process, would the work complete — or would they need someone to show them the real route?
text.senior_leader: Could a competent new joiner execute this workflow from the documented process alone, without informal transfer?

options.label: Yes — the written process is sufficient on its own
Mostly — a few small gaps they would pick up quickly
Not really — they would need significant coaching on the real route
No — following the written process alone would stall the work

items.scoringNote: Second input to mapInstructionVariance alongside os_d2_workaround_stability. The token official_and_actual_process_diverge is what the adapter tests for; do not rename. This item is the clearest single read on whether output depends on undocumented knowledge.

text.operational: The recurring reports you produce — do they drive a decision, or are they mostly for visibility?
text.managerial: Do the recurring reports your team produces actually drive decisions, or do they mostly satisfy visibility and compliance requirements?
text.senior_leader: Of the recurring reporting this environment generates, how much genuinely informs a decision rather than serving visibility or compliance?

options.label: Most of it drives an actual decision
A mix of decision-driving and visibility reporting
Mostly visibility or compliance rather than decisions
Honestly, it is unclear who uses some of them at all

items.scoringNote: Feeds the reportingTouches estimate in legacy-adapter.v1.js (mostly_decision_driving=2, mixed=3, mostly_visibility_or_compliance=5, unclear_who_uses_them=6). Tokens fixed by that mapping. Reporting nobody consumes is the cheapest burden to remove and the hardest to see from the top.

text.operational: Roughly how many hours a week do you personally spend on administrative upkeep — updating systems, chasing status, maintaining trackers — rather than the work itself?
text.managerial: Roughly how many hours a week does a typical person on your team spend on administrative upkeep rather than the work itself?
text.senior_leader: Roughly how many hours per week does a typical person in this environment spend on administrative upkeep rather than the work itself?

items.scoringNote: Numeric. deriveAdminHoursWeekly in legacy-adapter.v1.js prefers this explicit answer and only falls back to inferring from os_d6_upkeep_share when it is absent. The routing engine also already carries a burden curve for this exact id in numericBurdenScore. Single largest driver of the exposure model's annual-hours figure.

text.operational: Is the time you spend on administrative upkeep tracked anywhere, or does it just disappear into general capacity?
text.managerial: Is your team's administrative upkeep time tracked anywhere, or is it absorbed into general capacity?
text.senior_leader: Is administrative upkeep in this environment measured anywhere, or is it absorbed invisibly into general capacity?

options.label: Tracked and visible to the people who decide about resourcing
Partly visible — some of it surfaces, some does not
Not really — it disappears into general capacity
It is not formally tracked at all

items.scoringNote: Second input to mapDragVisibility alongside os_g4_drag_visibility; tokens hidden_in_general_capacity / not_formally_tracked / partly_visible / tracked_and_visible are read verbatim by the adapter. Drives the burden-profile 'hidden' shape, which is what separates an environment that knows its cost from one that does not.

text.operational: Of the work you handle, how much needs some kind of special handling rather than just following the normal steps?

options.label: Almost none — the normal steps cover it
A small share needs special handling
A sizeable share — it comes up most weeks
Most of it — special handling is basically the job

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d1_exception_ratio (managerial/senior only). Reuses that item's exact option tokens so deriveExceptionSteps in legacy-adapter.v1.js scores it with no change. The person handling exceptions observes their frequency more directly than their manager does.

text.operational: When something needs special handling, does it feel like an exception — or just like the way the work goes now?

options.label: It genuinely feels like an exception
It stopped feeling unusual a while ago
It is simply how the work goes now

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d3_exception_normalization. Same option tokens, so deriveExceptionSteps consumes it unchanged. Normalisation is a felt experience; the person inside the work is the only one who can report whether it still registers as unusual.

text.operational: Over the past year, have checks and approvals on your work been added, removed, or stayed about the same?

options.label: Some added, some removed — roughly balanced
Things get added; almost nothing gets taken away

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d5_control_add_remove_symmetry. Reuses that item's tokens (balanced / removals_are_rare / additions_outpace_removals) so mapControlBias scores it unchanged. Accumulation of checks is visible from below even when the governance rationale is not.

text.operational: When something is unclear or goes wrong, what usually happens next — a new check gets added, or someone fixes the underlying cause?

options.label: Someone sorts out the actual cause
Usually another check or sign-off appears
Almost always another check or sign-off

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d5_default_response_to_uncertainty (senior only). Reuses tokens add_control_first / nearly_always_add_control / clarify_or_redesign so mapControlBias scores it unchanged. Front-line staff are the ones who absorb the new check, so they observe the reflex most directly.

rules: Top 2 burden dimensions are stable and clearly separated from the rest.
Contradictions have been resolved or there are no unresolved contradiction flags.
Minimum depth requirements have been satisfied.
One additional item is unlikely to materially change the primary burden diagnosis or first intervention order.

stabilityDefinition.minimumSignals: At least two burden-bearing signals, or one high-weight numeric signal plus one confirming categorical signal.
stabilityDefinition.confidenceThreshold: Must exceed the threshold for the selected depth.
stabilityDefinition.rankStability: Rank position unchanged across the last two scoring updates unless a contradiction probe is still open.

burdenProfileShapes.concentrated: One burden dimension dominates. Emphasize focus and first-move leverage.
burdenProfileShapes.distributed: Multiple dimensions elevated together. Emphasize sequencing discipline and risk of burden displacement.
burdenProfileShapes.hidden: Formal signals may understate the real condition. Emphasize invisible labor, visibility gap, and calibrated uncertainty.

implementationPath.note: Feed the existing scoreOperationalSystems.js through a legacy-key adapter first, then rewrite the scorer to consume the new bank after parity is confirmed.

No behavior change from the cleanup: these references already no-op'd in the queue guard. Companion scorer change (same date): os_d1_routine_step_count now feeds process_density (it was asked and discarded), so runs answering it score differently than under the 2026_05_14 scorer — see scorer_version. | Prior 1.1.0 (30 Jul 2026): +9 items. Five the adapter and engine already expected but the config never defined (os_d2_workaround_stability, os_d4_new_person_viability, os_d3_report_actionability, os_d6_admin_hours_weekly, os_d6_upkeep_visibility), plus four front-line counterparts reusing their parent items' option tokens (os_d1_exception_frontline, os_d3_exception_frontline_norm, os_d5_control_frontline_growth, os_d5_uncertainty_frontline). Scoring arithmetic unchanged: identical answers to the 1.0.0 items still produce the identical 1.0.0 score.

text.operational: When work goes off the official path, is the workaround itself consistent, or does it depend on who is doing it that day?
text.managerial: When your team works around the official process, is that workaround consistent across people, or does each person improvise their own?
text.senior_leader: When work departs from the documented process, do people use a consistent workaround, or does it vary by person?

options.label: The official path is followed; no informal knowledge needed
There is a workaround, but everyone uses the same one
It varies noticeably from person to person
It is improvised more or less every time
The documented process and the way work is actually done no longer match

items.scoringNote: Feeds instructionVariance via mapInstructionVariance in legacy-adapter.v1.js, which reads this id directly. Option tokens are fixed by that mapping and must not be renamed. Dimension is workaround_dependence on substance; the d2 prefix is retained because the adapter references this exact id.

text.operational: If someone new joined tomorrow and followed only the written process, would they be able to complete the work?
text.managerial: If a new team member followed only the documented process, could they complete the work, or would someone need to show them how it is really done?
text.senior_leader: Could a capable new employee complete this workflow using only the documented process, without someone passing on unwritten knowledge?

options.label: Yes: the written process is sufficient on its own
Mostly: a few small gaps they would learn quickly
Not really: they would need substantial coaching on how the work is actually done
No: following the written process alone would stall the work

items.scoringNote: Second input to mapInstructionVariance alongside os_d2_workaround_stability. The token official_and_actual_process_diverge is what the adapter tests for; do not rename. This item is the clearest single read on whether output depends on undocumented knowledge.

text.operational: Do the recurring reports you produce lead to decisions, or are they mainly used to keep people informed?
text.managerial: Do the recurring reports your team produces lead to decisions, or mainly meet information-sharing and compliance requirements?
text.senior_leader: How much of the recurring reporting for the work you are examining informs decisions, rather than serving information-sharing or compliance needs?

options.label: Most reporting leads to a decision
A mix of reports that support decisions and reports that keep people informed
Mostly for information-sharing or compliance, rather than decisions
It is unclear who uses some of the reports

items.scoringNote: Feeds the reportingTouches estimate in legacy-adapter.v1.js (mostly_decision_driving=2, mixed=3, mostly_visibility_or_compliance=5, unclear_who_uses_them=6). Tokens fixed by that mapping. Reporting nobody consumes is the cheapest burden to remove and the hardest to see from the top.

text.operational: About how many hours a week do you personally spend on administrative maintenance, such as updating systems, following up on status, or maintaining trackers, rather than the work itself?
text.managerial: About how many hours a week does a typical person on your team spend on administrative maintenance, such as updating systems, following up on status, or maintaining trackers, rather than the work itself?
text.senior_leader: About how many hours a week does a typical person in this area of work spend on administrative maintenance, such as updating systems, following up on status, or maintaining trackers, rather than the work itself?

items.scoringNote: Numeric. deriveAdminHoursWeekly in legacy-adapter.v1.js prefers this explicit answer and only falls back to inferring from os_d6_upkeep_share when it is absent. The routing engine also already carries a burden curve for this exact id in numericBurdenScore. Single largest driver of the exposure model's annual-hours figure.

text.operational: How is the time you spend on administrative maintenance recorded and made available to the people who decide staffing and workload?
text.managerial: How is your team's time spent on administrative maintenance recorded and made available to the people who decide staffing and workload?
text.senior_leader: How is time spent on administrative maintenance in this area of work recorded and made available to the people who decide staffing and workload?

options.label: Recorded routinely and routinely available to those decision-makers
Recorded routinely, but not routinely available to those decision-makers
Informal estimates only; no routine records
Neither routine records nor informal estimates

items.scoringNote: Second input to mapDragVisibility alongside os_g4_drag_visibility; tokens hidden_in_general_capacity / not_formally_tracked / partly_visible / tracked_and_visible are read verbatim by the adapter. Drives the burden-profile 'hidden' shape, which is what separates an environment that knows its cost from one that does not.

text.operational: Of the work you handle, how much needs some kind of special handling rather than just following the normal steps?

options.label: Almost none: the normal steps cover it
A small share needs special handling
A sizeable share: special handling comes up most weeks
Most of it: special handling is effectively the job

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d1_exception_ratio (managerial/senior only). Reuses that item's exact option tokens so deriveExceptionSteps in legacy-adapter.v1.js scores it with no change. The person handling exceptions observes their frequency more directly than their manager does.

text.operational: In your team, to what extent has handling work outside the usual process become accepted as normal work rather than something to correct?

options.label: Accepted as normal work to a limited extent
Fully accepted as the standard way the job is done

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d3_exception_normalization. Same option tokens, so deriveExceptionSteps consumes it unchanged. Normalisation is a felt experience; the person inside the work is the only one who can report whether it still registers as unusual.

text.operational: Over the past year, have checks and approvals on your work been added, removed, or stayed about the same?

options.label: Some added, some removed: roughly balanced
Checks or approvals get added; almost none are removed

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d5_control_add_remove_symmetry. Reuses that item's tokens (balanced / removals_are_rare / additions_outpace_removals) so mapControlBias scores it unchanged. Accumulation of checks is visible from below even when the governance rationale is not.

text.operational: When something is unclear or goes wrong, what usually happens next: a new check gets added, or someone fixes the underlying cause?

options.label: Someone sorts out the actual cause
A mix of both, depending on the situation
Usually another check or sign-off appears
Almost always another check or sign-off

items.scoringNote: Front-line counterpart to os_d5_default_response_to_uncertainty (senior only). Reuses tokens add_control_first / nearly_always_add_control / clarify_or_redesign so mapControlBias scores it unchanged. Front-line staff are the ones who absorb the new check, so they observe the reflex most directly.

rules: Top 2 burden dimensions are stable and clearly separated from the rest.
Contradictions have been resolved or there are no unresolved contradiction flags.
Minimum depth requirements have been satisfied.
One additional item is unlikely to materially change the primary burden diagnosis or first intervention order.

stabilityDefinition.minimumSignals: At least two burden-bearing signals, or one high-weight numeric signal plus one confirming categorical signal.
stabilityDefinition.confidenceThreshold: Must exceed the threshold for the selected depth.
stabilityDefinition.rankStability: Rank position unchanged across the last two scoring updates unless a contradiction probe is still open.

burdenProfileShapes.concentrated: One burden dimension dominates. Emphasize focus and first-move leverage.
burdenProfileShapes.distributed: Multiple dimensions elevated together. Emphasize sequencing discipline and risk of burden displacement.
burdenProfileShapes.hidden: Formal signals may understate the real condition. Emphasize invisible labor, visibility gap, and calibrated uncertainty.

implementationPath.note: Feed the existing scoreOperationalSystems.js through a legacy-key adapter first, then rewrite the scorer to consume the new bank after parity is confirmed.

1.3.1.versionNote: 1.3.1 (9 Sep 2026): response-range clarification. The two middle administrative-time labels now use non-overlapping boundaries: 10% to less than 25%, and 25% to 40%. Item IDs, response values and order, burden signals, routing tags, weights, routing, scoring arithmetic and exposure calculations are unchanged. The exact deployed 1.3.0 bank remains registered for saved-run replay. | Prior 1.3.0 (8 Sep 2026): participant-language revision. Authorized exception-handling options now measure acceptance as normal work rather than mixing acceptance with frequency. Administrative-maintenance options distinguish routine records and decision-maker access, informal estimates only, and neither. Item IDs, response values and order, routing signals, weights, scoring arithmetic and exposure calculations are unchanged. Earlier and revised wording are distinct questionnaire versions; identical interpretation or participant responses are not assumed. The earlier archived bank remains unchanged for existing runs. | Prior 1.2.0 (8 Aug 2026): dead-branch cleanup + step-count wiring. Removed 2 rules whose entire inject lists referenced items that were never authored (os_g3_burden_trajectory -> [os_d3_reporting_growth, os_d6_burden_age]; os_d1_routine_step_count -> [os_d1_last_process_audit, os_d1_removability_test]) and pruned 4 more dead targets (os_d2_integration_quality, os_d3_reporting_growth, os_d4_key_person_absence_test, os_d5_control_removal_authority) from otherwise-live rules. No behavior change from the cleanup: these references already no-op'd in the queue guard. Companion scorer change (same date): os_d1_routine_step_count now feeds process_density (it was asked and discarded), so runs answering it score differently than under the 2026_05_14 scorer — see scorer_version. | Prior 1.1.0 (30 Jul 2026): +9 items. Five the adapter and engine already expected but the config never defined (os_d2_workaround_stability, os_d4_new_person_viability, os_d3_report_actionability, os_d6_admin_hours_weekly, os_d6_upkeep_visibility), plus four front-line counterparts reusing their parent items' option tokens (os_d1_exception_frontline, os_d3_exception_frontline_norm, os_d5_control_frontline_growth, os_d5_uncertainty_frontline). Scoring arithmetic unchanged: identical answers to the 1.0.0 items still produce the identical 1.0.0 score.

dimensions.label: Process Density
dimensions.description: Accumulated weight of steps, reviews, approvals, handoffs, and procedural requirements relative to what the underlying work requires.

dimensions.label: Systems Friction
dimensions.description: Labor and attention consumed by system switching, duplicate data entry, manual patching, and integration gaps.

dimensions.label: Reporting and Exception Burden
dimensions.description: Operating labor absorbed by reporting, oversight, proof-of-work demands, and exception handling.

dimensions.label: Workaround Dependence
dimensions.description: Degree to which execution depends on off-path effort, informal coordination, or improvised compensatory behavior.

dimensions.label: Control Load
dimensions.description: Cumulative governance weight relative to the actual risk profile and value of the work being controlled.

dimensions.label: Administrative Upkeep Burden
dimensions.description: Ongoing maintenance labor required simply to keep the administrative environment functioning.

notes.runtime_state_trigger: State keys resolve against the running engine state object and are evaluated after burden recomputation and before next-item selection.
notes.maxFirings: Scoped to the injected probe or item ID, not merely the routing rule.
notes.dedup: The engine deduplicates the queue by item ID before each render step.
notes.skipIfAnswered: If true, do not inject an item already answered earlier in the same run.

60.coverageRule: All six dimensions, deepest on top 3 active dimensions

text.operational: What most often slows down the work or creates extra effort?
text.managerial: What most often causes your team to lose time or do unnecessary administrative work?
text.senior_leader: What most often adds effort or delays to getting work done in this area of work?

options.label: Switching systems and entering the same information again
Administrative maintenance, such as maintaining systems and records

items.scoringNote: Primary burden source is the initial gating classifier and should activate the selected dimension immediately.

text.operational: Roughly how much of your working time goes toward administrative tasks rather than directly advancing the work itself?
text.managerial: Roughly how much of your team’s time goes toward administrative tasks rather than directly advancing the work itself?
text.senior_leader: Roughly how much working capacity in this area of work goes to administrative tasks rather than work that directly advances results?

items.scoringNote: High admin time share activates upkeep burden and may also indicate hidden reporting burden.

text.operational: Over the past year, has the administrative workload around your work become heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?
text.managerial: Over the past year, has the administrative workload around this workflow become heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?
text.senior_leader: Over the past year, has the administrative workload in this area of work become heavier, lighter, or stayed about the same?

items.scoringNote: Trajectory is a burden-age and growth signal rather than a direct burden dimension.

text.operational: Is the time spent on administrative work in this area of work generally visible to the people who could reduce it?
text.managerial: Is the time your team loses to administrative work generally visible to the people who could reduce it?
text.senior_leader: Is the working capacity used by administrative tasks in this area of work generally visible to the people with authority to reduce it?

items.scoringNote: Hidden drag visibility suppresses confidence and increases the chance of hidden burden profile classification.

text.operational: How many distinct approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine work item typically require before it is complete?
text.managerial: How many distinct approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine work item typically require in this area of work?
text.senior_leader: How many separate approval, review, or sign-off steps does a routine work item typically require in this area of work?

items.scoringNote: High step count is a direct process-density indicator.

text.managerial: How often does routine work need exception handling or escalation?
text.senior_leader: How common is exception handling compared with work that follows the normal steps in this area of work?

items.scoringNote: High exception ratio cross-loads into reporting and exception burden.

text.operational: How many separate systems or tools does a person typically use to complete one unit of work in this area of work?
text.managerial: How many separate systems or tools does your team typically use to complete one unit of work in this area of work?
text.senior_leader: How many distinct systems or tools are typically involved in moving one unit of work through this area of work?

items.scoringNote: System count increases friction exposure but should be interpreted together with design quality.

text.operational: How often does completing work require re-entering information that already exists somewhere else in the system?
text.managerial: How often does your team have to enter information again when it already exists elsewhere in the systems you use?
text.senior_leader: How often does this area of work require duplicate data entry across systems?

items.scoringNote: Duplicate entry is a direct signal of systems friction and may activate contradiction probe C3 in combination with low system count.

text.operational: How many hours per week does a typical person in this area of work spend on status reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?
text.managerial: How many hours per week does a typical team member spend on status reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?
text.senior_leader: How many hours per week does a typical person in this area of work spend on reporting, recurring updates, or administrative documentation?

items.scoringNote: High reporting hours are a primary direct measure of reporting burden.

text.managerial: In this area of work, to what extent has handling work outside the usual process become accepted as normal work rather than something to correct?
text.senior_leader: In this area of work, to what extent has handling work outside the usual process become accepted as normal work rather than something to correct?

options.label: Accepted as normal work to a limited extent
Fully accepted as the standard way the job is done

items.scoringNote: High exception normalization combined with flat trajectory activates chronic normalization contradiction logic.

text.operational: How often do people have to manually follow up just to keep work moving?
text.managerial: How often does your team have to manually follow up just to keep work moving?
text.senior_leader: How often does work in this area of work depend on manual follow-up just to keep moving?

items.scoringNote: Manual follow-up is one half of contradiction probe C1 and should remain distinct from off-path work.

text.operational: How often does getting work done require steps or contacts that are not part of the official process?
text.managerial: How often does your team rely on work outside the official process or informal coordination to get work done?
text.senior_leader: How often does this area of work depend on work outside the official process or informal coordination to maintain output?

items.scoringNote: High off-path work is a primary workaround dependence signal and pairs with manual follow-up in contradiction probe C1.

text.operational: For this work, does the effort required by oversight and controls feel proportionate to the actual risk or compliance need?
text.managerial: Does the effort required by oversight and controls around this work feel proportionate to the actual risk or compliance need?
text.senior_leader: Does the effort required by current oversight and controls seem proportionate to the actual risk and value of the work?

options.label: Much heavier than the risk warrants

items.scoringNote: Governance fit is the primary control-load proportionality test and one half of contradiction probe C2.

text.managerial: When new controls or oversight requirements are added, how often are existing ones removed to balance the additions?
text.senior_leader: When new controls or oversight requirements are added, how often are existing ones removed to balance the additions?

options.label: Additions and removals are regularly balanced

items.scoringNote: Control add/remove asymmetry is the bias half of contradiction probe C2.

text.senior_leader: When uncertainty arises, what does the organization usually do first?

options.label: Clarify the issue or redesign the work

items.scoringNote: Senior leader directional control-bias probe that can also surface C2 directly.

text.operational: How much of the weekly administrative workload here goes to keeping things running rather than advancing results?
text.managerial: How much of the weekly administrative workload in this area of work goes to keeping things running rather than advancing results?
text.senior_leader: How much of the weekly administrative workload in this area of work goes to keeping things running rather than advancing results?

options.label: Administrative maintenance takes more time than expected
Most of the workload is administrative maintenance

items.scoringNote: Upkeep share is the first direct burden framing question for D6.

text.operational: When work needs effort outside the official process, does that usually include follow-up steps missing from the formal process?
text.managerial: Does your team’s work outside the official process often include follow-up that the formal workflow would not record?
text.senior_leader: Could the informal effort keeping this workflow running be missing from formal workflow records?

options.label: No, the formal and informal routes are reasonably aligned

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for visible/invisible labor split.

text.operational: Even when the process seems broadly reasonable, is the usual response to uncertainty still to add another check, step, or approval?
text.managerial: Even when oversight seems proportionate, does this area of work still tend to add new oversight more readily than it removes old requirements?
text.senior_leader: Even when leaders describe oversight as proportionate, is the organization’s usual response to uncertainty still to add a control rather than redesign the workflow?

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for framing-versus-behavior gap in control load.

text.operational: If the number of systems is not especially high, is the real problem how those systems are designed, connected, or used in practice?
text.managerial: Do the difficulties come less from the number of systems and more from poor connections between them, poor workflow design, or people having to bridge the gaps manually?
text.senior_leader: Does the effort required by technology in this area of work come more from poor design and gaps between systems than from the number of systems involved?

items.scoringNote: Cross-item contradiction probe for design-quality versus system-count mismatch.

text.operational: Could the real burden here be heavier than it appears because some of the extra effort is simply treated as normal work?
text.managerial: Could your team be doing more administrative work than leadership can see because it is treated as part of normal delivery expectations?
text.senior_leader: Could the work required in this area of work be substantially greater than current measures suggest because administrative maintenance is missing from capacity estimates?

items.scoringNote: Scoring-layer contradiction probe. Evaluate only after burden recomputation and before next-item selection.

text.operational: Has this level of exception handling been part of the job long enough that it no longer stands out as unusual?
text.managerial: Has repeated exception handling become so accepted that the team treats it as normal work rather than a sign of a weak workflow?
